definition.def: If you assume that something is true, you imagine that it is true, sometimes wrongly.
examples: It is a misconception to assume that the two continents are similar. [VERB that]
If the package is wrapped well, we assume the contents are also wonderful. [VERB that]
If mistakes occurred, they were assumed to be the fault of the commander on the spot. [be VERB-ed to-infinitive]

definition.def: If someone assumes power or responsibility, they take power or responsibility.
examples: Mr Cross will assume the role of Chief Executive with a team of four directors. [VERB noun]
If there is no president, power will be assumed by the most extremist forces. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If something assumes a particular quality, it begins to have that quality.
examples: In his dreams, the mountains assumed enormous importance. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If you assume a particular expression or way of behaving, you start to look or behave in this way.
examples: He contented himself by assuming an air of superiority. [VERB noun]
Prue assumed a placatory tone of voice. [VERB noun]

definition.def: You can use let us assume or let's assume when you are considering a possible situation or event, so that you can think about the consequences.
examples: Let us assume those clubs actually win something. Then players will receive large bonuses.
Let's assume for a moment that I am a litigant in your court.
